title: Contemporary Scientific Racism in Psychology: “Cold Winters” Then and Now
abstract: Abstract I discuss persistent problems of conceptualizing and recognizing scientific racism in psychology, that is, “the use of scientific concepts and data to create and justify ideas of an enduring, biologically based racial hierarchy” (Winston, 2022). This formulation leaves a number of issues unexamined : first, the barriers in psychology to categorizing this academic work as a form of racism, especially due to the view of racism as a personal attribute; second, the difficulty of evaluating individual journal submissions when their relationship to a broader program and to political uses of scientific racism is unclear or obscured, and third, the recent trend to argue for or imply a racial hierarchy without using racial taxonomy or even mentioning “race.” I use the history of “cold winters theory” of group and regional differences in intelligence test scores to illustrate how the scientific racism community in psychology uses evolutionary discourse to revive and preserve long discredited and pernicious ideas.
